title: January 13
summary:
This document is a Wikipedia-style encyclopedia entry for the date **January 13**, describing it as the 13th day of the year in the Gregorian calendar, with 352 days remaining (353 in leap years). The article is organized into several main sections:

**Events:** A chronological listing of significant historical events that occurred on January 13, divided into three periods—Pre-1600, 1601–1900, and 1901–present. Notable entries include Octavian's transfer of the Roman state (27 BC), the Nika riots in Constantinople (532), the founding of the National Geographic Society (1888), the premiere events surrounding Émile Zola's "J'accuse…!" (1898), the Johnny Cash Folsom Prison concert (1968), the Air Florida Flight 90 crash (1982), the sinking of the Costa Concordia (2012), the first confirmed COVID-19 case outside China (2020), and Donald Trump's second impeachment (2021).

**Births:** An extensive catalog of notable people born on January 13, organized chronologically from ancient figures like Guangwu of Han through modern figures such as Liam Hemsworth, Connor McDavid, and other contemporary athletes, actors, politicians, scientists, and artists.

**Deaths:** A similar chronological list of notable figures who died on this date, ranging from Roman general Gaius Marius (86 BC) to modern figures including writer James Joyce (1941), Vice President Hubert Humphrey (1978), singer Teddy Pendergrass (2010), and others.

**Holidays and observances:** Religious and cultural commemorations associated with the date, including Christian feast days (Hilary of Poitiers, Mungo), St. Knut's Day, Constitution Day (Mongolia), Democracy Day (Cape Verde), Liberation Day (Togo), Old New Year's Eve celebrations in Eastern Europe, and South/Southeast Asian festivals such as Lohri and Bhogi.

The document concludes with **references** to scholarly sources and **external links** to "On This Day" resources from BBC and The New York Times.
